<subject>RE: Mumbai Market Update</subject>
<body>
I believe our conversation regarding an additional fee applicable to customers of all categories was related to our hypothesis on how the "new CTC" reimbursement mechanism might function, rather than Mumbai specifically. As far as I understand, the reimbursement mechanism remains theoretical. There are numerous possible options.

That’s how I remember it.

Ravi Sharma/AgriIndia@agribizXgate 24 May 2021 09:26 AM  
To: Sanjay Kulkarni/AgriIndia@agribizXgate  
Cc: Anil Desai; Priya Nair; Priya Nair; Neha Joshi  
Subject: RE: Mumbai Market Update

Sanjay, Anil, Priya, and I were on a trip with Mr. Rao last week. From my discussion with Anil, it seems Mr. Rao might believe that all customers, including Direct Access, should bear the increase you mentioned. Anil? This is promising from a risk mitigation perspective because if all consumers are treated equally, our Direct Access clients who were transitioned to bundled utility service cannot claim disadvantage from our actions. Conversely, if they must pay because they were placed back on utility service, they might attempt to pass those costs back to us. If any increase is intended to reimburse the state agency for power procurement from 01/02/2021 to 31/03/2022, and Direct Access customers are exempt, our company could face significant exposure to our clients. Perhaps we need to adjust our approach accordingly.

-----Original Message-----  
From: Sanjay Kulkarni  
Sent: Thursday, 24 May 2021 08:48 AM  
To: Anil Desai; Ramesh Patel; Kavita Singh; Ravi Sharma; Neha Joshi; Arjun Mehta  
Cc: Meera Kapoor; Neha Joshi; Rajesh Nair; Swati Mehta; Priya Nair  
Subject: Mumbai Market Update

The Mumbai Electricity Distribution Company’s filing confirms that the ABX143 tariff freeze at 6.5 INR/kWh does not cover Direct Access customers.

In hearings concerning the Distribution Company’s proposed tariff increase for large consumers:

- The company has proposed allocating all retained generation capacity to small consumers (below 100 kW). Large consumers would be served by the state authority or through Direct Access. Multiple stakeholders have expressed significant concerns about this.

- It is notable that the company’s calculated tariff increase under their proposal is 2.86 INR/kWh. If large consumers are allocated a portion of retained generation, the increase rises slightly to 2.99 INR/kWh. In that scenario, large consumers retain a CTC (related to power purchase agreements and other long-term stranded costs) that they would otherwise lose.

Our aim is to secure an order that: 1) excludes Direct Access customers from any tariff increase (the proposed 2.86 INR/kWh); 2) excludes Direct Access from any surcharge related to under-recovery during the tariff freeze (amount currently unknown); 3) prorates the surcharge related to under-recovery if the customer switches from Direct Access to bundled service during the freeze period; and 4) ensures a return to market pricing once the freeze ends.

The regulatory commission’s decisions on these matters are expected by 28 June. There is no discussion restricting movement between bundled service and Direct Access. Regarding our priorities, points 1, 2, and 4 have a strong likelihood of success; point 3 is about 50/50.

</body>
